newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Maradona wants to be journalist, interview Castro.
newsitem.headline: Maradona wants to be journalist, interview Castro.

text.p: Argentina's fading soccer star Diego Maradona said on Tuesday his new ambition was to trade his boots for a microphone and interview Cuban leader Fidel Castro.

"This has been my idea for a long time," the 36-year-old star of Argentina's 1986 World Cup victory told local radio. "I have an enormous desire to fly off to Cuba and conduct the first interview with the commander."
Maradona, an admirer of the Cuban communist leader, said he would also like to interview South African President Nelson Mandela.
"First I have got to retire from soccer," said Maradona, who signed for Buenos Aires' Boca Juniors last year but has not played for nearly three months.
During that time, he has admitted having a cocaine habit and his manager Guillermo Coppola has been jailed on drug-dealing charges.
Maradona has often announced his retirement from soccer only to make another comeback. But last week, after a rare training session he panted: "I haven't got the strength."
